clusters.name: Criterion A (Daily Sleepiness)
items: Recurrent irrepressible need to sleep, lapses into sleep, or napping within same day (DSM p.422)

clusters.name: Criterion B1 (Cataplexy)
items: Long-standing: brief bilateral muscle tone loss with laughter/joking (DSM p.422)
Children/early: spontaneous facial grimaces, tongue thrusting, global hypotonia without emotional trigger (DSM p.422)

clusters.name: Criterion B3 (Sleep Lab)
items: PSG REM latency <=15 min OR MSLT mean sleep latency <=8 min with >=2 SOREMPs (DSM p.422)

criteria.thresholds: Criterion A >=3 days/week for >=3 months; Criterion B >=1 of B1, B2, or B3 (DSM p.422)
subtypes: Narcolepsy Type 1 / NT1 (with cataplexy or CSF hypocretin <=110 pg/mL) (DSM p.422)
Narcolepsy Type 2 / NT2 (without cataplexy and normal/unmeasured hypocretin) (DSM p.422)
Secondary Narcolepsy (due to medical condition) (DSM p.422)

epidemiology.onset_age_typical: 15-25 years peak onset; 62% onset <18 years (DSM p.425; Dulcan p.483)
epidemiology.heritability: 25%-32% monozygotic twin concordance; 10-40x risk in 1st degree relatives (1%-2%) (DSM p.425-426)
comorbidities: Rapid-onset Obesity & Precocious Puberty in prepubescent onset (DSM p.425, 428)

etiology.genetic: HLA-DQB1*06:02 in 85-95% NT1 (DSM p.425-426); TCR-alpha gene polymorphisms (DSM p.426)
etiology.neurobiology: Autoimmune destruction of Orexin/Hypocretin neurons in lateral hypothalamus (LH); loss of OX1R/OX2R signaling to TMN (histamine) & LC (NE) (StahlNeuro p.406-407, 434)
etiology.environmental: Group A Streptococcal infection, pandemic H1N1 2009 influenza, Pandemrix vaccine, head trauma (DSM p.426)

first_line: Pitolisant (presynaptic H3 inverse agonist/antagonist, non-controlled, disinhibits histamine from TMN) (StahlNeuro p.404, 444)
Modafinil / Armodafinil (DAT inhibitors, enhance tonic dopamine & downstream histamine/orexin) (StahlNeuro p.442; Dulcan p.484)
Sodium Oxybate (GHB / GABA-B agonist, restores slow-wave sleep, FDA-approved for pediatric NT1/EDS/cataplexy) (Dulcan p.484; StahlNeuro p.446)
D-Amphetamine / Adderall (DAT/NET releasers, FDA-approved for narcolepsy age >=6) (StahlKids p.1, 17)
Methylphenidate (DAT/NET inhibitor, FDA-approved for narcolepsy) (StahlKids p.329; Dulcan p.484)
second_line: Scheduled naps (1-2 naps of 25-30 min) (Dulcan p.484)
key_side_effects: Stimulants: insomnia, appetite suppression, tachycardia, hypertension (StahlKids p.1, 17)
Sodium Oxybate: enuresis, sedation, nausea (Dulcan p.484; StahlNeuro p.446)
treatment.monitoring: BP, HR, weight/height for stimulants (StahlKids p.6); baseline cardiac history screening (StahlKids p.1)

items: CSF Hypocretin-1 <=110 pg/mL diagnostic for NT1 (DSM p.422, 424)
PSG REM latency <=15 min (nSOREMP) highly specific (95-97%) (DSM p.422, 424)
MSLT mean sleep latency <=8 min + >=2 SOREMPs (DSM p.422, 424)
Actigraphy for 7-14 days required prior to MSLT (Dulcan p.476; DSM p.424)
HLA-DQB1*06:02 genotyping for screening / negative predictive value (DSM p.425-426)
BEARS, Epworth (ESS-CH), PSQ, and CSHQ pediatric sleep questionnaires (Dulcan p.475)
key_numbers: <=110 pg/mL - CSF Hypocretin-1 cutoff for NT1 (DSM p.422)
<=8 minutes - MSLT mean sleep latency threshold (DSM p.422)
>=2 SOREMPs - minimum sleep-onset REM periods on MSLT (DSM p.422)
<=15 minutes - PSG nocturnal REM latency threshold (nSOREMP) (DSM p.422)
2 weeks - drug washout required before MSLT (DSM p.424)
7-14 days - actigraphy duration before testing (Dulcan p.476)

items: Idiopathic Hypersomnia: long unrefreshing sleep >10h, no SOREMPs, normal hypocretin (DSM p.420, 427; Dulcan p.484)
Insufficient Sleep Syndrome: false-positive SOREMPs via REM rebound (DSM p.424, 427; Dulcan p.476)
Obstructive Sleep Apnea: 25% comorbid, snoring/apneas on PSG (DSM p.425, 427)
Pseudocataplexy (Conversion): preserves intact deep tendon reflexes (no areflexia) (DSM p.428)
Pediatric ADHD: sleepiness masked as hyperactivity and behavioral problems (Dulcan p.483; DSM p.428)
Atonic Seizures: drop attacks without emotional trigger, abnormal EEG (DSM p.428)
key_numbers: >10 hours - sleep duration in Idiopathic Hypersomnia (DSM p.420, 427)
25% - OSA comorbidity rate in narcolepsy (DSM p.425, 427)
2 weeks - sleep extension trial duration to rule out insufficient sleep (DSM p.427)

high_yield: Pitolisant is a presynaptic H3 inverse agonist/antagonist that disinhibits histamine release from TMN and is NOT a controlled substance (StahlNeuro p.404, 444)
CSF Hypocretin-1 <=110 pg/mL is diagnostic for NT1 and is NOT altered by psychotropic medications or sleep deprivation (DSM p.422, 426)
In children, cataplexy often presents as static facial grimacing, tongue thrusting, or global hypotonia without emotional triggers (DSM p.422)
Sodium Oxybate acts on GHB/GABA-B receptors, restores slow-wave sleep (SWS), and is FDA approved for pediatric narcolepsy and cataplexy (Dulcan p.484; StahlNeuro p.446)
MSLT requires >=2 weeks of psychotropic drug washout (especially REM suppressants) to avoid REM rebound false-positive results (DSM p.424)
Areflexia during attacks distinguishes genuine cataplexy from pseudocataplexy/conversion, where reflexes remain intact (DSM p.428)
D-Amphetamine (Dexedrine Spansule) and Adderall are FDA-approved for narcolepsy in children aged >=6 years (StahlKids p.1, 17)
